title: The Four Porsches
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko, Agasa, Kogoro, Megure, Takagi, Jodie, Araide, Haibara) omitted by convention; this episode's parallel Black Organization/Haibara subplot (being tailed, Jodie/Vermouth driving Agasa and Ai home) does not touch the murder case's entity graph and is left out. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep338-339_the_four_porsches.json) already had the correct culprit (Taiyama) -- unlike several other rebuilt episodes, there is no culprit correction here. What it missed: the murder actually happened inside Kureko's Porsche 911 (Banba was sleeping off drunkenness in the passenger seat of Kureko's car, not his own), the fishing line was routed under Hotei's Porsche 356A (the middle-parked car) before running into the gap at the top of Taiyama's Boxster window and being tied to her gear lever -- her Boxster's power window is what supplied the pulling force, which is why Hotei's car (no power window) and Kureko's car (no line access) were ruled out despite both owning weapon-capable objects (an automatic fishing reel, a music box) found during the search, which were red herrings. The old file's backstory event (e1) also undersold the motive: Taiyama's brother died in a Ferrari that veered off a mountain road after Banba sprayed cold water at its occupants as a prank during an impromptu race; Taiyama herself was in the car and was rescued three hours later, while her brother was not. Banba later covered up his role by claiming to golfing buddies that he had merely witnessed the crash. case_type: murder.
